card.statement:
(1)

In [GT96, §2] and [SV13, Appendix A],
a similar formula was given.
Let us describe it in our notation.
For a fixed partition $\lambda$ we have

$\displaystyle(1-q)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mu\,\vdash|\lambda|-1\\
\mu\subset\lambda\end{subarray}}t^{1-i(s_{\lambda/\mu})}c_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)B_{s_{\lambda/\mu}}^{k}=h_{k+1}[(1-q)(1-t^{-1})B_{\lambda}-t/q].$

for $k\geq 1$ .
For the cases $k=\pm 1$ one can also show

$\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mu\,\vdash|\lambda|-1\\
\mu\subset\lambda\end{subarray}}t^{1-i(s_{\lambda/\mu})}c_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)B_{s_{\lambda/\mu}}^{\pm 1}=(1-t)e_{\pm 1}[B_{\lambda}].$

Here we used the symbol
$e_{-1}[X]:=\sum_{i}X_{i}^{-1}$ .
The formula for $k=-1$ seems to be a new one.

(2)

We also have a “higher-order analogue” of Lemma 3.3.
Instead of the case $|\lambda|=|\mu|+1$ ,
we now consider the case $|\lambda|=|\mu|+d$ for any $d\geq 1$ .
The result is given in a generating function form.
For a fixed partition $\mu$ , we have

$\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\lambda\,\vdash|\mu|+d\\
\lambda\supset\mu\end{subarray}}q^{n(\lambda^{\prime})-n(\mu^{\prime})}d_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)\dfrac{1}{\prod_{i=1}^{d}(1-uB_{s_{\lambda/\mu}^{(i)}})}$
$\displaystyle=\dfrac{\prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-uY_{k})}{\prod_{k=1}^{m+d}(1-uX_{k})}\dfrac{1}{\prod_{k=1}^{d}(1-t^{k})}$

$\displaystyle=\prod_{k=0}^{d-1}\dfrac{\widetilde{E}_{\mu}[u/t^{k}]}{1-t^{k+1}}.$

In the first part,
$\{s_{\lambda/\mu}^{(i)}\mid i=1,\ldots,d\}$ is the boxes
consisting of the skew Young diagram $\lambda/\mu$ .
For defining the variables $X_{k}$ , $Y_{k}$ in the second part,
let us label from left to right and from top to bottom
by $s_{1},s_{2},\ldots,s_{m+d}$ the attachable boxes to $\mu$
so that $\lambda/\mu$ forms a vertical strip.
Here $m$ is some non-negative integer.
Then define

$X_{k}:=q^{j(s_{k})-1}t^{1-i(s_{k})}=B_{s_{k}}\ (1\leq k\leq m+d),\qquad Y_{k}:=q^{j(s_{k+d})-1}t^{1-i(s_{k})}\ (1\leq k\leq m).$

We show an example for $\mu=(6,6,4,3,3,1,1,1)$ and $d=3$ in Figure 3.

Figure 3. Boxes $s_{k}$ for $\mu=(6,6,4,3,3,1,1,1)$ and $d=3$ .

The function $\widetilde{E}_{\mu}[u]$ in the last part
is defined to be

$\widetilde{E}_{\mu}[u]:=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(-u)^{r}e_{r}[(1-q)(1-t^{-1})B_{\mu}-1]=\dfrac{1}{1-u}\dfrac{\prod_{s\in\lambda}(1-uB_{s})(1-uB_{s}q/t)}{\prod_{s\in\lambda}(1-uB_{s}q)(1-uB_{s}/t)}.$

This formula seems to be a new one, so we mentioned it.
The proof is similar, so we omit it.

3.2. Part 2 of the proof

In this subsection we show the condition

$\displaystyle D_{d}v_{n}^{(0)}=0\quad(d\geq 2)$

in Corollary 2.6.
Let us recall some notations.

$\displaystyle v_{m}(0)$
$\displaystyle=v_{m}^{(0)}=\sum_{\lambda\vdash m}J_{\lambda}(q,t)\dfrac{q^{n(\lambda^{\prime})}}{\langle J_{\lambda}(q,t),J_{\lambda}(q,t)\rangle_{q,t}},$

$\displaystyle\quad D(z)$
$\displaystyle=\sum_{d\geq 0}D_{d}z^{-d}=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n>0}(1-q^{n})\partial_{p_{n}}z^{-n}\Bigr).$

paper.title: Whittaker vector of deformed Virasoro algebra and Macdonald symmetric functions
paper.abstract: We give a proof of Awata and Yamada's conjecture for the explicit formula of Whittaker vector of the deformed Virasoro algebra realized in the Fock space. The formula is expressed as a summation over Macdonald symmetric functions with factored coefficients. In the proof we fully use currents appearing in the Fock representation of Ding-Iohara-Miki quantum algebra. We also mention an interpretation of Whittaker vector in terms of the geometry of the Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane.
